brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
A Tujia speciality of Shizhu county in Chongqing, made from glutinous rice rather than tea leaves and closer to a sweet snack than a brew.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
history: It is recorded in the Qing-era local gazetteer of Shizhu. Each winter, households steam, sun-dry, rub and shade-dry the new glutinous rice, then fry it in lard and boil it with sweet fermented rice, often adding poached eggs. Little more is documented about it.
processing: Glutinous rice is steamed, sun-dried, rubbed and shade-dried; to serve, it is fried in lard and boiled with sweet fermented rice.
harvest_season: The rice is prepared each winter from that year's crop.
appearance_liquor: Depends on the plant; usually pale to amber.
taste_profile: A herbal infusion; the taste depends on the plant.
vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
